> **These notes are unfinished intentionally.** Students will help build them as we document our work.

## Personal identity

Start with the person before the product. What experiences, interests, places, communities, skills, values, and goals shape how you see yourself?

The goal is not to reduce identity to a logo. It is to notice what matters enough to communicate.

## Group identity

Groups also develop identity through shared stories, symbols, colours, language, routines, and expectations.

A useful design question is:

**What should someone understand or feel when they encounter this group?**

## From identity to visual identity

Personal and group identity give us material for visual communication. We will eventually turn that thinking into marks, logos, typography, colour, and motion.

That becomes the foundation for **Unit 3: Logo Design & Animation**.
